name: countbyte
algorithm: doc/reference.md section 7's CountByte block: count the bytes equal to b in n bytes, 16 lanes at a time (splat b, load 16 bytes, compare, count the set lanes of the mask), then a scalar tail; reps passes over n bytes generated by splitmix64 from seed, pass r counting b = r % 256; the checksum is the wrapping sum of each pass's count times (r % 1000 + 1) (README.md).

skip.rust: lang-sys's row (plan/29-sys.md 6): the reference's CountByte block against C's SSE2 version, to show the std.simd lowering is vector code; std-simd's SIMD rows carry every language
skip.zig: lang-sys's row (plan/29-sys.md 6): the reference's CountByte block against C's SSE2 version; std-simd's SIMD rows carry every language
skip.go: lang-sys's row (plan/29-sys.md 6): the reference's CountByte block against C's SSE2 version; std-simd's SIMD rows carry every language

no_counts: B24 does not apply as a count of operations: the work per pass is fixed by n, and the checksum weights each pass's count by its position, so a kernel that counts any byte value wrongly changes it
notes: Mk: the reference block CountByte, unchanged, over std.simd (Vec[u8, 16].Splat, FromSlice, ==, Mask.CountSet); mk-wrap: the same with the count's += written as +% (B4). C: the same loop with SSE2 intrinsics (_mm_set1_epi8, _mm_loadu_si128, _mm_cmpeq_epi8, _mm_movemask_epi8) and the vector layer's _mm_popcnt_u32 (BS-8). Every column is built for each variant's cpu, x86-64-v2.

Sizes (B16): L1 16 KiB, L3 32 MiB, DRAM 1 GiB. GB/s counts n * reps bytes, each pass reading the whole buffer. The fill (one splitmix64 pass) and its first-touch page faults are timed by each variant's baseline (reps 0) and subtracted (BS-3). Only x86-64-v2: the block is fixed at 16 lanes, so at x86-64-v3 every column would run the same 16-byte loop (C's intrinsics are SSE2), and std-simd's rows carry the v3 widths.

Aligned buffers (BS-4): the c column's buffer starts on a 64-byte boundary, and it exits 3 if not. The mk and mk-wrap columns read an arena slice (sys.arena.Slice[u8]) whose alignment Mk code cannot set or read without std.raw, which the SIMD table bans (an unsafe module); this is the labelled exception of tests/bench/README.md (as validutf8's mk column), until std's aligned allocation reaches Arena (plan/29-sys.md S-1).

Checks: Mk's FromSlice checks 0 <= i <= len - 16 once per load (plan/29-sys.md 4.4), which LLVM removes under the loop condition i + 16 <= len, and the mk column's n += is overflow-checked; mk-wrap drops that check, so mk / c includes its price and mk-wrap / c does not. C checks nothing.

The checksums were computed by a byte histogram of the same input (sum over passes of hist[r % 256] * (r % 1000 + 1)), which reproduces the row's first checksums (1284639 and 102502750000 at 65536 bytes), and confirmed by go run ./tools/bench verify (status/lang-sys.md, fix round).
Written by the lang-sys lane (status/lang-sys.md, session 2; variants, mk-wrap, BS-4 and BS-8 in the M6 review fix round).
